newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon ceasefire monitors condemn Israeli shelling.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon ceasefire monitors condemn Israeli shelling.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon on Thursday condemned Israeli shelling of south Lebanon villages in which one Lebanese civilian was killed and two others wounded two days ago.

The group comprising the United States, France, Syria, Israel and Lebanon condemned the act which consisted a breach of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April.

"The monitoring group unanimously condemned the shelling on February 18, 1997 which affected the villages of Habbouch, Arab Salim and Kfar Rummane," the group said in a statement issued after the meeting.

"It expressed serious concern at the killing of a Lebanese woman, as a result of military action by Israeli forces or those cooperating with them and considered them as responsible for the manner in which they conducted their firing," the statement added.

The monitors said the Israeli delegation defended the firing as a self-defence act against launching sites in the south Lebanon villages. The Lebanese delegation rejected the claim and stated that the firing was deliberately aimed at civilian populated areas, the statement said.

The April agreement bans Israel and Hizbollah from firing from or at civilian targets bur reserves the pro-Iranian guerrillas the right to fight Israeli troops inside a 15 km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone.
The deal also grants both parties the right to self-defence.
Hizbollah leads an Islamic Resistance committed to ousting Israeli troops and their local militia allies from south Lebanon.

The monitoring group, which met at the headquarters of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) in the coastal village of Naqoura inside the security zone, urged combatants to comply with the provisions of the April 26 understanding.

Last Tuesday, Israeli and allied militia forces shelled the three south Lebanon villages, killing Naeemeh Hallal, in her 30s, and wounding two other civilians, Lebanese security sources said. The government complained to the monitoring group.
Pro-Israeli militia sources said the bombardment was in retaliation for guerrilla shelling of three posts of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia in the zone.

In its reaction to previous similar Lebanese complaints over Israeli shelling, the monitors deplored the Israeli action and expressed deep regret over the civilian injuries but fell short of condemning Israel.
